sw_cafe_lady.text: Soup, scone, and a cup of tea you could stand a spoon in. There's a bannock fresh out the oven. A bere bannock, with barley from the machair. Warm, with butter. It's a plain thing and the best plain thing there is.
Tì? Say tapadh leat when it comes and you'll get the bigger scone. That's not a rule. That's me.

sw_tweed_gossip.text: Mind, my mother wove tweed in the shed. Click-clack, click-clack. Every house had a loom, I thought everyone's mother did. It was a shock to move to Glasgow and find people with no click-clack at all.

Mothers waulked the cloth too, thumping it on a table with their hands and feet, singing òran luaidh, waulking songs, to keep time and to pass the work. If you don't know a few verses, you're not from round here, or you're from Edinburgh.
